findings.current: Sometimes, what you’ve always taken for granted goes wrong.
findings.defect: The source’s opening only says that such moments sometimes happen in life; the next sentence supplies the unexpected turn. This line adds that things “go wrong” and repeats the taken-for-granted idea from the following sentence.
findings.rationale: The source separates the general setup (line 5) from the unexpected turn (line 7). The assembled opening makes the setup more negative and duplicates the following sentence’s premise.
findings.replacement: Sometimes, life throws you a curveball.

findings.current:
I wanted that to be the case.

I wished I were. Unfortunately, this was real.
findings.defect: The assembled English repeats the wish before stating that reality is different. The source expresses the wish once, followed by the contrast.
findings.rationale: The source says he wished he were dreaming or in an illusion, but the truth was different. “I wished I were” repeats the preceding sentence rather than translating another source beat.

findings.current: I seized the Skeleton King’s wrist.
findings.defect: The source says the narrator grabs the wrist while speaking urgently. The assembled English omits that urgency.
findings.rationale: The source’s “다급한 목소리와 함께” explicitly conveys urgency as he grabs the wrist; the accepted baseline also preserves it.
findings.replacement: I seized the Skeleton King’s wrist, my voice urgent.

summary: The translation contains a duplicated thought, adds a negative implication to the opening, and drops the narrator’s urgency when he grabs the Skeleton King.
